title: Post-event pipeline: from capture to consumption
tagline: The post-event stage records a room in depth, then almost nothing reads the record. This project makes every run finish loudly and route what it learned.
bottomLine: The pilot and the first build are done. Every post-event run now leaves a ledger of what ran and ends with a close-check that prints PASS or FAIL. On 11 November the Rooms step was cut and the router build got the go-ahead. The router is now in progress: it is being proven on the Agentics brief first, so the backfill of undebriefed rooms gets routed instead of adding more unread briefs.
healthReason: The 3 December target holds with no open blocker: both pending decisions were made on 11 November. It turns at-risk if the routing block can't be parsed reliably on the Agentics brief (due 14 November).
why: A systems review of the 4 November Agentics Spotlight run found that post-event is strong at capture and weak at consumption. The brief ran to about 20,000 words across 17 sections, and only two things read it: one round of posts and the graph's claim extraction. The glossary, tools, anecdotes, open loops, unused angles and follow-up state had no reader. The worst failures were also silent: the command itself noted that a skipped graph write still closed green, and a stalled session lost track of which steps had run.
mission: Every post-event run leaves a ledger of what ran, ends with a check that reads the real state and prints PASS or FAIL, and routes each section of the brief to something that acts on it: an issue, a project idea, a follow-up, a story, a content backlog row.
destination: Attending a room reliably turns into finished, checked work: posts, follow-ups on a date, build ideas, interview stories and graph claims. Done means three things: the close-check passes or skips with a reason on every new run, routed items are closed at a measurable rate after 30 days, and debrief coverage rises as the backfill runs.
showcase: Running a failure-mode analysis (FMEA: severity × occurrence × detection) on a live pipeline and ranking fixes by how silently each failure happens
A write-ahead run ledger and a read-only close-check, so a stalled or skipped step shows up instead of closing green
A manual pilot before automating: one brief routed by hand to prove which outputs get used before writing the router
Every metric reported against its do-nothing baseline, including the ones that are still zero

milestones.title: Systems review of the post-event stage (consumption audit + robustness and value analysis)
milestones.note: Two proposals: where each brief section should go, and a ranked list of failure modes with a sequenced plan.

milestones.title: Manual routing pilot on the Agentics brief
milestones.note: One brief produced five tracked follow-ups: a target-list decision, an upskilling task, two dated second touches and a content backlog item.

milestones.title: Privacy fix: post-event working files are private by default
milestones.note: Working files in each event's post-event folder are ignored unless they are a rendered carousel. A CI check that enforces this is a next step.

milestones.title: Run ledger, close-check and agent preflight
milestones.note: 51 tests. The first live close-check on Agentics printed FAIL (2).

milestones.title: Brief routing block and router step, with a lite debrief mode and one event name derived from Notion
milestones.note: Uphill until the routing block parses cleanly on the Agentics brief. After that it is plumbing.

milestones.title: Themes and content plan on every post-event post, plus X cuts
milestones.note: Clears the Themes failure in the close-check for every future run.

milestones.title: First routed batch of the backfill of undebriefed rooms
milestones.note: Runs after the router, so every backfilled room is routed rather than adding another unread brief.

milestones.title: Interview prep reads the rooms you were in

metrics.label: Post-event steps verified at the end of a run
metrics.note: Graph event row, claims, themes, the Themes property on posts, routing rows, and run-state gaps. The Rooms check was removed on 11 November.

metrics.label: Agentics close-check
metrics.baseline: Not measurable before the check existed
metrics.target: All pass or skipped with a reason
metrics.note: Passing: graph event, 118 claims, 5 themes, run-state. Failing: the Themes property on the post. Skipped: routing rows, which the router will write.

metrics.label: Routing yield (routed items closed ÷ created)
metrics.note: Three days in, from one brief. The spec judges routing yield at 30 days, so this is not yet a result.

metrics.label: Attended rooms with a post-event debrief
metrics.note: Counted from event folders, which include some virtual and pending entries; the true denominator needs the calendar. Moves only once the backfill runs.

decisions.decision: Route every brief section to a reader instead of adding new sections to the brief.
decisions.why: Nothing in the review needed more capture. Everything needed a reader.

decisions.decision: Pilot the routing by hand on one event before building the router.
decisions.why: A manual pass shows which outputs actually get used, for the cost of an afternoon instead of a build.

decisions.decision: Build the run ledger and close-check first.
decisions.why: The two highest-risk failures were silent ones (risk scores 80 and 64), and a check that prints FAIL is the cheapest detection.

decisions.decision: The close-check reports and never blocks a run.
decisions.why: No wired hook may block a turn. A loud FAIL fixes the silence without stalling the pipeline.

decisions.decision: Build the router before the backfill.
decisions.why: Backfilling without routing would only add more long briefs that nothing reads.

decisions.decision: Cut the Rooms tab and the per-run Rooms entry from post-event.
decisions.why: No entries had been added since 28 September, so the check failed on every run. Room pages stay up because long reads, themes and published links point into them. A room entry is now added only when a long read is made.

decisions.decision: Start the router and lite debrief build now.
decisions.why: Routing has to exist before the backfill, or the backfill only adds more unread briefs.

Review and merge the router PR

assumptions.assumption: The synthesizer can write a routing block consistent enough to parse without hand fixes.
assumptions.test: Parse it on the Agentics brief. If more than 1 item in 10 needs a hand fix, the router proposes and a person confirms.

assumptions.assumption: Routed follow-ups get worked, not just filed.
assumptions.test: Routing yield at 30 days (7 December) against a baseline of 0. Routes with no closed items get cut.

assumptions.assumption: A lite debrief (recap, recording summary, three claims) is worth having when a full brief isn't.
assumptions.test: Run one event both ways and compare the claims and follow-ups each produces.

risks.risk: Event names are typed by hand, so one event can end up with two slugs, as Agentics already has. A batch backfill would multiply this.
risks.mitigation: Derive the slug once from the Notion title, in the same PR as the router.

risks.risk: Routed follow-ups pile up unworked, which moves the reading gap from the brief to the issue tracker.
risks.mitigation: Judge routing yield at 30 days and cut the routes that nobody works.

log.text: Rooms cut from post-event and the hub nav. Router build started.
